# Core updates

*Update* · also written core update

Broad changes to Google's ranking systems, announced several times a year, that reassess content quality across the web.

**Glossary** (*Core update*): A significant, broad change to Google's ranking systems, made several times a year and announced on the Google Search Status Dashboard. Core updates do not target specific sites and are not penalties.

Narrative: the topic [Core updates and spam updates](../topics/search-updates.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

28 claims mention it: 6 from Google's documentation, 20 shown or said at the event (4 not in Google docs, 6 confirmed by Google docs, 10 consistent with Google docs), 2 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Google Search's core updates and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/updates/core-updates), [Google Search Status Dashboard](https://status.search.google.com/products/rGHU1u87FJnkP6W2GwMi/history).

- [`D3-C261`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Docs: As of 3 October 2026, the Ranking history of Google's Search Status Dashboard lists two core updates in 2026 (March and May) and four spam updates (March, June, August and September). `[D3-C261, docs, Google Search Status Dashboard (Ranking incident history), https://status.search.google.com/products/rGHU1u87FJnkP6W2GwMi/history]`
- [`D3-C266`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Docs: Google's 2019 post on core updates says Google tests any broad core update before it goes live, including feedback from its search quality raters, whose data is not used directly in ranking. `[D3-C266, docs, Search Central blog (1 August 2019), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2019/08/core-updates]`
- [`D3-C272`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Docs: Google's core updates page recommends waiting at least a full week after a core update has finished rolling out before analysing Search Console data, then comparing that week with a week before the update started. `[D3-C272, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/updates/core-updates]`
- [`D3-C273`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Docs: Google's core updates page says a small drop in position after a core update (for example from 2 to 4) needs no drastic action, while a large drop (for example from 4 to 29) calls for a deeper assessment. `[D3-C273, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/updates/core-updates]`
- [`D3-C295`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Docs: Google's core updates page says improvements can take effect in a few days but may take several months for its systems to confirm that the site as a whole produces helpful content, sometimes only at the next core update. `[D3-C295, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/updates/core-updates]`
- [`D3-C296`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Docs: Google's core updates page says Google also makes smaller core updates that are not announced, and these can also lift a site that has improved. `[D3-C296, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/updates/core-updates]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D3-C265`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Google sometimes couples a core update with an update to its Search Quality Rater Guidelines. `[D3-C265, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C270`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: To improve a site after a core update, check whether users can complete their information journey on the site and ask users directly, for example with customer satisfaction (CSAT) surveys, then improve based on the answers. `[D3-C270, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C661`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Slide, Day 3, not in Google docs: Google estimated that a core update affects a site within 2 to 4 weeks from the beginning of its rollout. `[D3-C661, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C705`](../sessions/D3-S18-wrapping-all-up-ai-search-and-making-sense-of-everything.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Search has changed every year since its start, for example the Florida update in 2003 (before core updates existed), Universal Search and the Knowledge Graph. `[D3-C705, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C259`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Several times a year Google makes significant, broad changes to its search algorithms and systems, which it calls core updates. `[D3-C259, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C260`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google announces core updates when they happen by posting them on the Google Search Status Dashboard. `[D3-C260, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C262`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Core updates do not target specific sites; they change how Google assesses certain properties of content. `[D3-C262, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C263`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: A core update may reward pages that were previously under-rewarded, so when some pages go down after a core update, other pages must go up. `[D3-C263, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C268`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Answering the common question whether to fix individual pages or the whole site after a core update, Google advised taking a close look at the site as a whole and trying to be objective. `[D3-C268, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C269`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Because owners struggle to judge their own site objectively, the speaker suggested asking someone else to review the site after a core update drop. `[D3-C269, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C244`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's slide said the more people post on the internet, the more saturated topics become and the harder it gets to find the highest quality content, so Google might launch core updates to improve the quality and relevance of search results. `[D3-C244, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C250`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Every kind of Search update, whether a feature launch, a core update or a spam update, has the same goal: satisfying users' information needs with better results. `[D3-C250, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C258`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google stressed that core updates are not punitive: they are not meant to punish any site but to improve how results are surfaced. `[D3-C258, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C264`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Pages that perform worse after a core update usually do not violate Google's spam policies; Google has changed, perhaps slightly, how it thinks about quality. `[D3-C264, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C267`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: The purpose of core updates is to improve the quality and relevance of search results for users. `[D3-C267, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C293`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: A ranking drop after a core update is not a penalty, so technically there is no recovery from a core update in the way there is after a spam update. `[D3-C293, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C294`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: After a core update a site can win back some of its rankings by improving the site as a whole. `[D3-C294, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C297`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: A drop after a core update can simply mean that a competitor now does better because Google rethought how it assesses quality as a whole. `[D3-C297, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C298`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's 'Recoveries' slide advised sites affected by a core update to keep doing a great job, look at what competitors are doing better and learn from sites that are doing better. `[D3-C298, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C662`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Recovery after a core update typically takes 3 to 6 months once the site has put in work to regain traffic, and up to 6 months to a year, until the next core update. `[D3-C662, slide, Google, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D3-C299`](../sessions/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) Analysis: After a core update drop, plan a site-wide quality review instead of page-by-page fixes or a technical 'recovery': have someone outside the team assess the site, compare it with the pages that gained, and test whether users can finish their task, for example with short satisfaction surveys. `[D3-C299, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C664`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Analysis: Set expectations for recovery work: a manual action can lift within weeks of a real clean-up, but recovery from a core update typically takes 3 to 6 months and may need the next core update, so do not judge quality work within the first weeks. `[D3-C664, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
